shots.say: It's picnic day! But the picnic spot is on the other side of the stream.
I'm Milo! Can you help my friends get to the picnic?
This is Mango, the spider monkey. And this is Tumble, the baby elephant.
Let's fill a basket with fruit, and have a picnic together!
A picnic with my friends! Yummy! Let's go!
What do we need for a picnic? A basket, or a bed?
The best fruit grows high up in the big tree. Up goes Mango!
Mango wraps her tail round the branch. And she hangs upside down!
A spider monkey's tail can hold up her whole body. So both her hands are free to pick fruit!
shots.tag: fact: the tail holds her, hands free

shots.say: How many fruits is Mango holding? Count with me! One, two!
One for Tumble. One for Milo. And one more for me!
Plop, plop, plop! Three fruits drop into the basket.
I'll carry the basket on my back. Off to the stream!
Off they go, through the green jungle.
Tumble carries the basket. Mango swings ahead, from vine to vine.
Here is the stream. And there is the picnic spot, on the other side!
The water is too wide to jump. How can we get across?
The vine bridge! I can swing across, easy peasy!
Spider monkeys have long arms and hook-like hands. They swing through the trees!
But I can't swing, Mango. I'm an elephant!
The bridge is low and short. But it goes wiggle, wobble!
Tumble puts one foot on the bridge. Wobble! He steps back.
Oh! It wiggles! I'm not sure about this, Mango.
Is the bridge still, or is it wobbly?
Watch me, Tumble! I'll take the basket over. Here I go!
Mango runs onto the bridge, fast, fast, fast. Boing! The bridge bounces!
Oh no! The basket tips over. The fruit rolls out on the grass.
Oops! I went too fast. I'm sorry, Tumble.
Tumble helps. He picks up the fruit with his trunk. Count with me! One, two, three!
All three are back in the basket. Phew!
My turn. I'll try it all by myself.
One step, two steps. Wobble, wobble, WOBBLE! Back he goes.
It wobbles too much when I go alone.
Milo flies over. Easy for a bird! But elephants cannot fly.
Can an elephant fly? Yes, or no?
Tumble sits down by the stream. Maybe there will be no picnic today.
You go without me, Mango. I can't do it.
Mango sits down next to Tumble. Tumble's tail droops low.
No, Tumble. A picnic is no fun without you.
What can good friends do? Go alone, or help?
Hmm. I went too fast. And I did not hold on.
I know! My tail can hold the vine, like an extra hand!
A spider monkey's tail can grab and hold, like an extra hand.
shots.tag: fact: the tail grabs like a hand

shots.say: I hold the vine with my tail. I hold your trunk with my hand. And we go slow, side by side.
Slow, and together? Okay. Let's try!
One step, two steps, slow and steady. Hold on tight, and here we go. Ready?
Count the steps with me! Three, four, five, six!
The bridge gives a little wobble. But Mango holds on tight, and so does Tumble.
Seven, eight, and hop! They made it across!
I did it! No, we did it, together!
You tried again, Tumble. You were so brave!
At last, the picnic! A blanket in the sun, and a basket of fruit.
How many fruits are on the blanket? Count with me! One, two, three!
One for Tumble, one for Milo, and one for me. Yummy!
Thank you for walking with me, Mango.
And thank you for trying again, Tumble.
Back at the zoo, the sun is low. And Mama is waiting.
Mama! I crossed the wobbly bridge, with Mango!
You tried again, Tumble. And Mango slowed down to help. I am so proud of you both.
Mama wraps her trunk around Tumble. A big, warm trunk hug.
When a friend feels wobbly, we can slow down, and go together.
Do you remember? What did Mango hold the vine with? Her tail, or her ear?
And how did they cross the bridge? Fast, or slow?
One step, two steps, slow and steady. Hooray, hooray, the picnic was ready!
Next time: who took Mango's breakfast? See you on the next adventure, friends!
